LESSON: WRITING 2.3.1 SOCIAL WRITING – CARDS

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.3: Writing 2.3.1 Social writing – Cards

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 2.3.1 Social writing – Cards. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why do we present cards to people?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the key components of a card for information

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: WRITING 2.3.1 SOCIAL WRITING – CARDS
This lesson teaches Writing 2.3.1 Social writing – Cards for Grade 8 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

STUDY STEPS
1. identify the key components of a card for information
   Practise this until you can do it without help.

HOW TO SHOW UNDERSTANDING
Explain the idea in your own words, give one Kenyan example, then complete the practice tasks.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Describe Writing 2.3.1 Social writing – Cards using something at your school.

Example 2: Give a home/community example from your county.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Underline the key ideas about Writing 2.3.1 Social writing – Cards above.
2. Explain Writing 2.3.1 Social writing – Cards to a parent using one local example.
3. Write or draw three things that prove you understand Writing 2.3.1 Social writing – Cards.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Writing 2.3.1 Social writing – Cards with school or home examples.
2. Answer: Why is Writing 2.3.1 Social writing – Cards important for a Grade 8 learner?
3. Prepare a one-minute oral presentation for a parent or teacher.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do we present cards to people?
2. How can we make cards more appealing when designing them?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify the key components of a card for information

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
